title: The 10 best NFL player matchups to watch in Week 1
completenessNotes: Public PFF article was accessible in full and exhausted. Analyst attribution, player-level matchup mechanisms and historical matchup evidence were captured where materially useful. No side, total, prop, score prediction or conviction was inferred.

records.game: San Francisco 49ers at Los Angeles Rams
records.construction: Rams edge rush vs 49ers left tackle
records.detail: Myles Garrett vs Trent Williams is identified as a game-swinging trench matchup. In their 2025 meeting Garrett generated four pressures and a sack on 14 head-to-head matchups with Williams; Locker says a repeat could materially sway the game toward Los Angeles.
records.implication: incremental Rams pass-rush leverage; qualitative only

records.game: New England Patriots at Seattle Seahawks
records.construction: Seattle WR1 vs New England CB1
records.detail: Jaxon Smith-Njigba vs Christian Gonzalez is framed as the premier Seattle receiving matchup. In Super Bowl LX, Smith-Njigba recorded one catch for 16 yards on 14 direct matchups but was charted open six times, creating tension between box-score suppression and underlying separation.
records.implication: adds route-level evidence to the existing Seattle passing-game matchup; no wager inferred

records.game: New England Patriots at Seattle Seahawks
records.construction: New England WR1 vs Seattle CB1
records.detail: A.J. Brown vs Devon Witherspoon is a new matchup element in the rematch. Brown is coming off a down 2025 by his standards, while Witherspoon finished as PFF's highest-graded corner; this is their first career head-to-head meeting.
records.implication: supports Seattle coverage resistance against New England's upgraded receiving corps without establishing a side

records.construction: Houston edge rush vs Buffalo left tackle
records.detail: Danielle Hunter vs Dion Dawkins is highlighted after Hunter generated four pressures when aligned against Dawkins in the 2025 meeting; Dawkins allowed two sacks in that game, his season high. Locker identifies Dawkins neutralizing Hunter as a key condition for Buffalo's offense in Joe Brady's head-coaching debut.
records.implication: incremental Houston pass-rush mechanism that is directionally consistent with existing Houston-side matchup evidence

records.construction: Atlanta WR1 vs Pittsburgh boundary coverage
records.detail: Drake London vs Jamel Dean is presented as Atlanta's marquee passing-game matchup. London owns an elite multi-year receiving grade profile, while Dean allowed a 47.7 passer rating when targeted in 2025; Joey Porter Jr. may also share London coverage if active.
records.implication: adds Atlanta perimeter receiving leverage/coverage context; no side or prop inferred

records.construction: Baltimore edge rush vs Indianapolis left tackle
records.detail: Trey Hendrickson vs Bernhard Raimann is flagged as a central trench matchup. Hendrickson had two sacks and six pressures on 23 matchups against Raimann in 2023, while Raimann has since posted three straight 82.0-plus overall PFF grades.
records.implication: adds specific Baltimore pass-rush upside but also acknowledges a materially improved Indianapolis tackle baseline

records.construction: Chicago WR1 vs Carolina outside coverage
records.detail: Luther Burden III vs Mike Jackson Sr. is highlighted as a meaningful Week 1 matchup. Burden averaged 2.34 yards per route run as a rookie, while Jackson posted an 85.8 coverage grade and allowed 55-plus yards in only three games in 2025; Jaycee Horn also factors into the coverage plan.
records.implication: adds a resistance point to Chicago's WR1 matchup rather than an automatic Bears passing-game advantage
